correctness.rationale: Homogeneity and a C2 Taylor expansion give the nonpositive quadratic necessity. Adding a smooth proper strictly decreasing converse Lyapunov function to a weak positive quadratic proves sufficiency and Morse Hessian. Quartic derivative is exactly negative sixth-power sum, giving GAS for all real couplings. Fourfold symmetry averages all candidate Hessians to a scalar; the perfect-square identity gives an attained sharp 2sqrt(2) cutoff including endpoints. The packaged SymPy checks reproduce critical polynomial identities and Hessian.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Jongeneel covers hyperbolic GAS via smooth Morse construction but this family is nonhyperbolic with zero Jacobian. Liu–Fitzsimmons family has radial polar drift of second harmonic and proves absence of polynomial Lyapunov in a different regime; ours has exact strict quartic, so that stronger polynomial nonexistence theorem is not applicable. Standard quadratic averaging is not claimed alone.

originality.rationale: Jongeneel 2610.05626v1 gives a weaker center-semismiplicity necessity and a nilpotent no-Morse example, not this iff criterion for homogeneous GAS systems. Liu–Fitzsimmons 2607.16171v1 excludes all polynomial Lyapunov functions for a different cubic, inapplicable to a family with a strict quartic for every coupling. The nearest published mathematical record concerns two fields with equal infinite Taylor jets; it neither establishes a homogeneous criterion nor the sharp C4-cubic threshold. Targeted alias, equivalence and literature searches found no dominant implication; originality is best-knowledge and not independently certified.

value.rationale: The motivating October 2026 paper leaves Morse sufficiency open for nonhyperbolic semisimple cases. This exact criterion completely resolves the homogeneous GAS subclass in all dimensions; the fourfold-symmetric cubic gives a natural sharp one-parameter boundary separating Morse smooth certificate existence from absence while retaining GAS and a strict polynomial quartic certificate on both sides. The exact nontrivial threshold is an attained natural invariant, not a routine model slice or rounding of a prior bound.
